cowlevel · Oct 24, 2026

HTTP 1 is full of parser differential vulnerabilities, which 2 fixes. That is probably its biggest flaw.

SMTP is too chatty - it uses too many round trips for efficient transfer across the internet. It can take several seconds just to get to the point of sending the email data. It also duplicates information between the SMTP envelope and the email body which creates vulnerabilities when they don't match.

For APIs that don't have to work in a browser I suggest JSON lines over TCP, or over TLS.

Every user is different

For me I'm a text-only user not interested in graphics

I do not use a so-called "modern" browser to make HTTP requests

I don't request brotli-compressed content/resources^1

Normally I don't send an Accept-Encoding header

Almost always servers to which I connect^2 will return uncompressed text, which is what I want. No Accept-Encoding header needed

Occasionally servers will send gzip-compressed text by default and will ignore "Accept-Encoding: identity"

However the popular so-called "modern" browsers will send an Accept-Encoding header whose value includes brotli (br) by default

Unsuspecting www users are consequently opted in to Google's brotli experiment. Me, I opt out

1. I use a text-only browser (1.3MB static binary) to read HTML. I compile it without brotli support
